q: The Production Linked Incentive scheme for the pharmaceuticals covers:
options: the bulk drugs of the public sector undertakings
new drugs, generics and complex generics with an emphasis on the research and development
the marketing and the distribution of the medicines
only the generic medicines exported to Africa
explanation: The PLI for the pharmaceuticals covers the new drugs, the generics and the complex generics and the formulation, with a significant portion of the incentive linked to the research and the development and the new product approvals.

q: The Production Linked Incentive scheme for the electronics covers:
options: the consumer electronics of the imported brands only
the semiconductor fabrication plants only
the assembly of the televisions of the foreign brands
the mobile phones, the specified electronic components and the IT hardware
explanation: The PLI for the electronics manufacturing covers the mobile phones, the specified electronic components and the IT hardware, and it is administered by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology.

q: The Production Linked Incentive scheme for the advanced chemistry cell is linked to:
options: the electric vehicle and the advanced chemistry cell manufacturing with the localisation of the value chain
the telecom equipment of the 5G networks
the export of the speciality steel
the bulk drug formulation
explanation: The ACC battery PLI supports the manufacturing of the advanced chemistry cells and the electric vehicles with a high degree of the localisation of the value chain.

q: The Production Linked Incentive scheme for the textiles and the apparel focuses on:
options: the processing of the imported fabric for the re-export
the spinning capacity of the cooperative mills
the cotton of the traditional handloom sector only
man-made fibre, technical textiles, speciality textiles and the apparel with the emphasis on the exports
explanation: The textiles and the apparel PLI covers the man-made fibre, the technical textiles, the speciality textiles and the apparel with a focus on the exports and the creation of the employment.

q: The Production Linked Incentive scheme for the white goods covers:
options: only the air conditioners and the refrigerators
the televisions and the home appliances of the import
refrigerators, air conditioners, washing machines and the LED lighting
the kitchen appliances of the unorganised sector
explanation: The white goods PLI covers the refrigerators, the air conditioners, the washing machines and the LED lighting with the focus on the local manufacturing and the export.

q: The Production Linked Incentive scheme for the food products covers:
options: the primary processing of the pulses and the oilseeds
the milk and the dairy, the tea, the coffee, the eggs, the meat, the marine, the fruits and the vegetables, the spices, the packaged food and the ready to eat items
only the export of the rice and the wheat
the cold storage and the warehousing alone
explanation: The food processing PLI covers the milk and the dairy, the tea, the coffee, the eggs, the meat and the marine, the fruits and the vegetables, the spices, the packaged food and the ready to eat food products.

q: The 'ZED' certification scheme of the Bureau of Indian Standards:
options: is a mandatory pre-shipment inspection of the textiles
is the quality standard for the defence equipment of the public sector
certifies the export worthy quality products of the small and the micro enterprises
certifies the organic produce of the exporters
explanation: The ZED certification is a quality and performance certification for the products of the small and the micro enterprises that enables them to compete in the export markets with the zero defect products.

q: The 'Udyam' registration for the micro, small and medium enterprises is:
options: a registration required only for the export oriented units
a mandatory registration under the Companies Act
a licence issued by the Ministry of MSME after the inspection
a self declaration based registration that replaced the earlier Udyog Aadhaar and the PAN based registration
explanation: The Udyam registration, introduced in July 2020, is a self declaration based and paperless registration that replaced the Udyog Aadhaar and the PAN based registration of the MSMEs.

q: The 'National Optical Fibre' project aims to:
options: connect every gram panchayat with the high speed internet and provide the digital infrastructure for the e-governance
replace the mobile broadband in the cities
lay the undersea cables in the Indian Ocean
provide the leased line connectivity to the defence establishments only
explanation: The National Optical Fibre project of the BharatNet aims to provide a fibre connection to every gram panchayat and to strengthen the digital infrastructure for the e-governance and the education and the health services.

q: The 'Dedicated Freight Corridor' projects of India are:
options: the Ludhiana to the Mundra and the Delhi to the Kandla routes
the Eastern corridor from Ludhiana to Kolkata and the Western corridor from Delhi to Mumbai
the Chennai to the Delhi and the Mumbai to the Kolkata routes
the Chennai to the Visakhapatnam and the Pune to the Kochi routes
explanation: The Dedicated Freight Corridors are the Eastern corridor from Ludhiana to Kolkata and the Western corridor from Delhi to Mumbai, and they are aimed at a faster and a cheaper freight movement with the double stack containers.

q: The 'Parvatmala' scheme of the road ministry is intended for:
options: the ropeways in the hill and the pilgrim destinations to improve the last mile connectivity
the construction of the ropeways for the tourist circuit of Kerala only
the maintenance of the existing cable cars of the tourism department
the ropeway network in the plains for the freight movement
explanation: The Parvatmala Pariyojana aims to develop the ropeways at the hill and the pilgrim destinations to provide the safe and the affordable mobility and to improve the last mile connectivity.

q: The 'garbage-free city' certification under the Swachh Bharat Mission-U is given to:
options: the cities that have the largest urban population
the cities with the maximum number of the public toilets
the cities with the highest municipal revenue
the cities that have declared themselves ODF plus the waste processing certification
explanation: The garbage free city certification under the SBM-U requires the declaration of the ODF status along with the verification of the solid waste processing and the disposal by the third party audit.

q: The 'source separation' of the waste:
options: has been stopped after the certification of the cities
is a key component of the sustainable waste management in the urban local bodies
is done only by the private concessionaires
is mandatory only for the commercial establishments
explanation: The source separation of the waste into the wet, the dry and the inert fractions at the household level is the key component of the sustainable waste management under the SBM-U, and it is verified by the third party audit.

q: The 'e-Courts' project of the judiciary:
options: replaces the interpreters in the court proceedings
digitises only the records of the Supreme Court
provides the electronic filing of the cases, the digital cause lists and the video conferencing in the courts
automates the judgement writing in the criminal cases
explanation: The e-Courts project of the National Judicial Data Grid enables the electronic filing of the cases, the digital cause lists, the e-filing of the appeals and the video conferencing, and it has been operational in the district courts since 2007.

q: The 'Agriculture Infrastructure Fund' provides the interest subvention for the post harvest infrastructure with a loan of up to:
options: Rs 2 crore for a period of seven years
Rs 5 crore for a period of five years
Rs 1 crore for a period of three years
Rs 10 crore for a period of ten years
explanation: The Agriculture Infrastructure Fund offers a 3 per cent interest subvention for a loan of up to Rs 2 crore for a period of seven years for the post harvest management infrastructure and the community level assets.

q: The 'Integrated Scheme for Agricultural Marketing' (ISAM) was formulated in:
options: 1995, with the creation of the e-NAM
2005, with the launch of the MSP procurement
2015, replacing the APMC reform programme
2020, to be implemented from 2021-22 with the continuation of the existing sub-schemes
explanation: The ISAM of 2020 subsumes the sub-schemes of the Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure, the Marketing Structure Reform, the Krishi Value Chain Development and the e-NAM with the scheme to continue from 2021-22.

q: The 'Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana' was restructured in 2018 as:
options: the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana
the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund
the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana with the focus on the integrated farming system and the value chain
the Kisan Call Centre and the Agritech Portal
explanation: The RKVY was restructured in 2018 with the focus on the integrated farming system, the value chain, the food processing and the agri-entrepreneurship with the States free to choose the sub-schemes.

q: The 'Seed Bill' proposed in India seeks to:
options: make the seed companies eligible for the export subsidy
replace the Seeds Act of 1966 and include the farmers in the registration of the varieties
increase the subsidy on the certified seed
abolish the seed certification of the private sector
explanation: The Seed Bill proposes to replace the Seeds Act of 1966, to bring the seed varieties in the registration and to provide the farmers the right to register their own varieties and to store and sell the seed of their choice.

q: The 'Contract farming' under the Model Agricultural Produce Market Contract Act, 2020:
options: requires the registration of every contract with the state
bans the multi-season contracts
permits the producer to sell to any person including the trader, the wholesaler and the retailer
allows the buyer to purchase only from the mandi
explanation: The Model Act provides for the freedom to sell to any person including the trader, the wholesaler, the retailer, the exporter and the consumer, and it allows the multi-season contracts with the sowing of the seed by the farmer.

q: The 'Food Corporation of India' procures the foodgrains for the:
options: the seeds and the fertilisers of the States
the procurement of the sugarcane of the mills
the export of the rice and the wheat only
the central pool and the distribution under the Public Distribution System
explanation: The FCI procures the foodgrains from the farmers for the central pool and the public distribution and the other welfare schemes, and it also undertakes the storage, the transportation and the distribution.

q: The 'Export-Import Bank of India' finances the exports and the imports of:
options: the Indian buyers and the buyers of the Indian goods abroad
the state trading corporations
only the central government
the overseas subsidiaries of the Indian companies
explanation: The EXIM Bank provides the financing for the Indian importers of the capital goods and for the buyers of the Indian goods abroad, and it offers the buyer's credit, the supplier's credit and the lines of credit for the countries.

q: The 'Forward Contract' in the foreign exchange market:
options: is a contract with the central bank for the purchase of the foreign currency
fixes the rate of exchange for a future date with an obligation to deliver the currency
is a spot purchase of the currency for immediate settlement
is an unconditional option to buy the currency at a future date
explanation: A forward contract is an agreement to buy or sell a currency at a fixed rate on a future date with the obligation to deliver the currency on that date, and it is used for the hedging of the exposure to the exchange rate.

q: The 'Interest rate differential' between India and the United States affects the:
options: the fiscal deficit of the States
the rate of the domestic inflation directly
the flow of the short term portfolio capital and the pressure on the rupee
the volume of the sea trade only
explanation: A wide interest rate differential in favour of the United States pulls the short term portfolio capital towards the dollar assets and puts a pressure on the rupee, and the carry trade in the forex market is based on this differential.

q: The 'Trade in Services' in India's Balance of Payments includes:
options: only the tourism and the pilgrimage receipts
travel, transportation, financial, computer, communication, construction and the business services
the freight and the insurance premiums alone
the software exports and the tele services only
explanation: The services trade covers the travel, the transportation, the financial, the computer and the information, the communication, the construction and the business services, and the net exports of the services are a large contributor to the current account surplus of the country.

q: the inflation of the current period is:
options: the inflation is calculated only from the food prices
the inflation is measured from the base year prices only
the price indices of the base year are revised every year
the inflation of the current period is partly a carry over of the price level of the corresponding period of the previous year
explanation: The base effect arises when the price level of the corresponding month of the previous year is unusually high or low, and it mechanically influences the year on year inflation of the current period.

q: The 'Weighted median inflation' used by the RBI:
options: gives more weight to the items of the household consumption of the poorer sections, so that the inflation of the vulnerable is captured
is the average of the CPI and the WPI
excludes the food prices from the computation
is the inflation measure of the corporate sector
explanation: The weighted median inflation gives a higher weight to the items of the consumption basket of the poorer households, and it is used along with the headline CPI as a measure of the inflation that affects the vulnerable.

q: The 'Supply inflation' in India is largely caused by:
options: the fiscal deficit of the States
the food and the fuel prices and the supply chain constraints
the excess demand in the economy
the expansion of the money supply alone
explanation: The food and the fuel components dominate the weights of the CPI in India, and the supply side disruptions of the pandemic and of the global edible oil and the fertiliser prices drove the supply inflation.

q: The 'Core inflation' in the Indian context excludes:
options: the manufactured goods prices
the housing component of the CPI
the services prices only
the food and the fuel components from the CPI
explanation: The core inflation is the inflation of the CPI excluding the food and the fuel, and it is used to gauge the underlying trend of the demand driven price pressures.

q: The 'multidimensional poverty in India is measured by:
options: the calorie consumption of the rural households only
the income of the top ten per cent of the population
the three dimensions of the health, the education and the living standards with the ten indicators
the per capita income of the States
explanation: The Indian multidimensional poverty index uses the three dimensions of the health, the education and the living standards with the ten indicators, and a household is multidimensionally poor when at least one of the three dimensions is deficient.

q: The 'Code on Social Security, 2020' provides for the gig workers the:
options: life and disability cover, accident insurance and the health and the maternity benefit with the contribution of the platform and the worker
a statutory minimum wage fixed by the Centre
a provident fund cover that is compulsory for every platform worker
a pension of Rs 3,000 to every gig worker above fifty years of age
explanation: The Code on Social Security provides the life and disability cover, the accident insurance and the health and the maternity benefit for the gig and the platform workers with a shared contribution from the platform, the aggregator and the worker.

q: The 'Periodic Labour Force Survey' in India provides the estimates of the:
options: the agricultural productivity of the crops
the wages of the unorganised sector alone
the migration of the workers to the cities
the labour force participation, the unemployment and the employment with the quarterly and the annual reports
explanation: The PLFS of the National Statistical Office provides the estimates of the labour force participation rate, the unemployment rate and the worker population ratio with the quarterly bulletins and the annual reports.

q: The 'employment in the agriculture sector' in India:
options: is entirely covered by the organised sector employment
is the smallest share of the workers
still accounts for the largest share of the workers though its share in the gross value added has declined
has ceased to be a source of the disguised unemployment
explanation: The agriculture sector continues to employ the largest number of workers in India, even though its share in the gross value added has fallen, and the disguised unemployment of the family farms is still a debated issue.
